data.gender_notes: Hezekiah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From Hebrew hizqiyahu, meaning 'God will strengthen'. In the Old Testament, Hezekiah was a king of Judah who reigned during a time of political and religious crisis. Hezekiah was a faithful and courageous leader who trusted in God to save him and his people. The name Hezekiah carries the meaning “God will strengthen” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hezekiah usually hope their child will grow to embody god will strengthen and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing trust in God's strength and protection.
data.etymology: Hezekiah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God will strengthen.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hezekiah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: חזקיהו
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים יחזק אתו - אלוהים הוא החוזק שלו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חזקיהו הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים יחזק אתו' או 'אלוהים הוא החוזק שלו'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'חזק' שפירושו 'לחזק' או 'להיות חזק', ו-'יהו' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם חזקיהו מופיע במקרא כמלך יהודה, בן של מנשה וסבו של מנשה.

in_greek.name: Ἐζεκίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἐζεκίας (Ἐζεκίας) ἐστὶν ὄνομα ἑβραϊκόν, ὃ σημαίνει 'ὁ Θεός ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ' ἤ 'ὁ Θεός ἐστιν ἡ ἰσχύς αὐτοῦ'. Τὸ ὄνομα ἀποτελεῖται ἀπὸ δύο λέξεις: 'חזק' (ἐζέκε) ποὺ σημαίνει 'ἀποκαθιστώ' ἤ 'κράταιος', καὶ '-ίας' (-ίας) ποὺ σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Ὁ Ἐζεκίας τῆς Βίβλου ἦν βασιλεὺς Ἰουδαίας, υἱὸς Μανασῆ.

in_latin.name: Hezekiah
in_latin.long_meaning: Hezekiah nomen hebraicum est, quod significat 'Deus est fortitudo eius' vel 'Deus est robur eius'. Nomen constat ex duabus vocibus: 'chazaq' quod significat 'confirmare' vel 'fortis', et '-iah' quod significat 'Deus'. Hezekiah in Biblia fuit rex Iudaeae, filius Manasse.

in_english.name: Hezekiah
in_english.meaning: God is his strength or God strengthens
in_english.long_meaning: Hezekiah is a Hebrew name that means 'God is his strength' or 'God strengthens'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'chazaq', meaning 'to strengthen' or 'to be strong', and 'yah', meaning 'God'. In the Bible, Hezekiah was a king of Judah, known for his faithfulness and trust in God. The name Hezekiah has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person who relies on God's strength and guidance. It symbolizes spiritual fortitude and trust in divine providence.

data.cultural_impact: Hezekiah is remembered in Jewish and Christian history for his efforts to restore the temple, maintain religious observance and obedience to God, and strengthen Judah's military defenses against foreign invasions. His rule marked a period of renewed national pride and unity in Judah.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hezekiah holds great significance for those who choose it as it serves as a reminder of God's strength and faithfulness. The name symbolizes trust in God to provide strength and protection, especially during difficult times. It also highlights the importance of remaining faithful to God and maintaining a strong spiritual foundation, as demonstrated by King Hezekiah's reign.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hezekiah means "God will strengthen." This name symbolizes God's unwavering support and strength in times of adversity. It is a reminder that even in the face of challenges, God is always present and providing the necessary power to overcome.

biblical_reference.note: Hezekiah was a king of Judah who reigned from around 727 to 698 BCE. He is known for his religious reforms and his trust in God during the Assyrian invasion.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that 2 Kings 18:1-12, 2 Chronicles 29-32 The name Hezekiah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hezekiah was a king of Judah who reigned during the Assyrian crisis. He initiated a religious reform, repairing the Temple and centralizing the worship of Yahweh.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Isaiah 38-39 The name Hezekiah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hezekiah, gravely ill, was given a sign by Isaiah that he would recover if he went up to the temple and prayed. He did so, and his illness was healed. Shortly after, Sennacherib of Assyria invaded Judah, but was defeated, and Hezekiah was spared.
